articles.title: Van Hollen says he wouldn’t reject DSA endorsement, but ‘certainly not seeking’ one
articles.summary: Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.) on Sunday did not shoot down a possible endorsement from the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), but the Democratic lawmaker added that he “certainly isn’t seeking it.” “I’m not going to sort of look into all these endorsements. I’m not going to reject an endorsement by certain individuals at the…
articles.body:
Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.) on Sunday did not shoot down a possible endorsement from the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), but the Democratic lawmaker added that he “certainly isn’t seeking it.”

“I’m not going to sort of look into all these endorsements. I’m not going to reject an endorsement by certain individuals at the DSA. But I’m certainly not seeking the endorsement from the DSA,” Van Hollen told NBC News’s Kristen Welker on “Meet the Press.”

The Maryland senator added that he believed that the recent debate among Democrats about the DSA “is an effort by Republicans” attempting “to reduce, you know, the turnout for Democrats.”

“I don’t think it’s going to work, because at the end of the day what unites Democrats is economic populism, standing up for working people,” he continued.

In the last few months, democratic socialist and progressive candidates have racked up wins in Democratic primaries against more establishment and moderate candidates. Van Hollen backed one of those candidates , Abdul El-Sayed, a Democratic candidate for Senate in Michigan.

Other more moderate Democratic lawmakers have bristled at the democratic socialist and progressive candidates , including Rep. Jared Moskowitz (D-Fla.) and Sen. John Fetterman (D-Pa.).

On Thursday, Moskowitz went after left-wing streamer Hasan Piker and DSA members, saying the two “can’t coexist with me.”

“Well, I mean, we’re going to see if we can coexist with them. I mean, they can’t coexist with me.” Moskowitz told Fox Business Network’s Stuart Varney on “Varney & Co.” while discussing Piker and the DSA.

”They targeted me months ago to try to take me out in a district that Trump won by nine,” he said, referring to President Trump’s 2024 win. “So, that was clear there. They weren’t interested in winning the general election in my seat. They were interested in just taking out a Democrat.”

Van Hollen on Sunday also repeated that he’s “ kicking the tires ” on a 2028 White House run, which he previously revealed on a podcast in June.

articles.title: Turning Point USA announces Charlie Kirk memorial on university campus where he was shot
articles.summary: Turning Point USA announced that its co-founder Charlie Kirk will be honored at a Sept. 10 event on the Utah Valley University campus, just feet from where he was shot. The event is titled “Freedom Built to Last” and will feature remarks from Turning Point USA spokesperson Andrew Sypher, conservative talk show host Glenn Beck…
articles.body:
Turning Point USA announced that its co-founder Charlie Kirk will be honored at a Sept. 10 event on the Utah Valley University campus, just feet from where he was shot.

The event is titled “Freedom Built to Last” and will feature remarks from Turning Point USA spokesperson Andrew Sypher, conservative talk show host Glenn Beck and Christian apologist Frank Turek.

“Utah Valley University seeks to foster healing for our community following the assassination of Charlie Kirk,” the university said in a statement sent to Nexstar, The Hill’s parent company.

“While campus operations will be closed that day to provide time and space for reflection, service, and connection, the UCCU Center will remain open. Turning Point USA has engaged Utah Valley University to use the UCCU Center on September 10 for a private event,” they added.

The UCCU center is a five-minute walk from the place where Kirk was assassinated in front of a crowd of students, supporters and Turning Point USA staff.

His wife, Erika Kirk, has continued her husband’s mission of spreading conservatism on college campuses by participating in a nationwide tour entitled “This Is the Turning Point Tour” after Kirk was killed during a stop on the “American Comeback Tour.”

Next month’s event honoring Kirk will kick off the “All-American Comeback Tour,” which will consist of additional stops on college campuses.

“UVU will continue listening, collaborating, and taking the time to thoughtfully support the needs of our campus community,” the university said in a statement ahead of the Sept. 10 event.

Talks are ongoing about holding a consistent memorial for Kirk in future years.

articles.title: Hakeem Jeffries and Jared Kushner meet in NYC to discuss how Democrats and Trump could cooperate
articles.summary: The meeting comes with just months to go before midterm elections that will determine control of Congress for the remainder of Trump’s term.
articles.body: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., recently met privately with Jared Kushner, President Donald Trump’s son-in-law and informal adviser, and they discussed possible areas of cooperation, a source familiar with the meeting confirmed to NBC News. The private meeting, which was first reported by The New York Times, took place in Manhattan, the source said. The meeting was an unusual instance of a top Democrat and a close Trump confidant coming together to discuss common ground. Jeffries, the top Democrat in the House, is one of Trump’s most prominent critics. Meanwhile, Kushner is a close relative of Trump’s and has taken on a slate of high-profile foreign policy issues as special envoy. The source, who was granted anonymity without being authorized to speak about the private meeting, did not share details about when it took place or what was discussed. The Times reported that it happened “in recent weeks,” citing five sources with knowledge of the meeting. The Times also reported that the pair discussed “housing, immigration and the high cost of living,” citing two sources with knowledge of the meeting. The meeting space in New York was “offered up by a mutual friend of the two men,” the newspaper reported, citing two people with knowledge of the meeting and a third who was briefed on it. Jeffries said in a statement Sunday that Republicans have adopted a “my-way-or-the-highway approach” that he said Democrats have made it clear “will not work and will be met with forceful opposition.” “In every conversation that we have with the Trump administration, we will continue to make it explicitly clear that the affordability crisis is not a hoax and nothing short of transformational policy change is acceptable. We are fighting for an affordable America. The question is whether Republicans will join us,” Jeffries said. The White House did not immediately respond to NBC News’ request for comment on the meeting. Despite their different policy perspectives, Jeffries and Kushner previously joined forces to champion a criminal justice reform bill during Trump’s first term. Kushner championed the bill, which Jeffries signed on to as a co-sponsor, giving it a bipartisan boost. The legislation, dubbed the First Step Act, was signed into law in 2018. The recent meeting, though, comes as both parties are entering the final stretch of the campaign season before midterm elections, when Democrats hope to flip the House and the Senate. If Democrats flip even a single chamber, it could significantly stymie any future legislative initiatives from the administration. If Democrats take back the House majority in November, Jeffries is the favorite to become the next speaker. He has predicted victory in the midterm elections, and he and his committee leaders have vowed to conduct aggressive oversight of the Trump administration on a range of issues, including ICE tactics, Trump’s Qatari-donated jet, his family business dealings and the White House ballroom. Kushner remains a close confidant of Trump. He was a senior adviser in the White House during Trump’s first term, and he is currently special envoy for peace missions, focused largely on the Middle East and the Russia-Ukraine war, along with another special envoy, Steve Witkoff.

articles.title: Jennings shrugs off reports about interest in press secretary job: ‘I don’t know what’s gonna happen’
articles.summary: Scott Jennings on Sunday downplayed reports that he is a favorite to succeed Karoline Leavitt as White House press secretary. “I don’t know what’s going to happen,” Jennings said on CNN’s “State of the Union.” The CNN contributor added, “I don’t have anything to say about it this morning,” before calling Leavitt “one of the…
articles.body:
Scott Jennings on Sunday downplayed reports that he is a favorite to succeed Karoline Leavitt as White House press secretary .

“I don’t know what’s going to happen,” Jennings said on CNN’s “State of the Union.”

The CNN contributor added, “I don’t have anything to say about it this morning,” before calling Leavitt “one of the best press secretaries in the … modern era.”

CNN reported Thursday that Jennings, who worked for former President George W. Bush and has advised Sen. Mitch McConnell (R-Ky.), was an early favorite for the press secretary gig.

During the 2024 presidential campaign and throughout President Trump’s second term, Jennings has frequently defended the president’s policies and decisions during appearances on CNN and while hosting his eponymous radio show.

Jennings and White House chief of staff Susie Wiles recently met at Mastro’s Steakhouse in Washington, D.C., according to CNN . The outlet noted that multiple White House staffers believe Jennings has backing from Wiles.

While Jennings deflected about his interest in the job, he praised Leavitt and Arkansas Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders (R), as the latter was Trump’s press secretary during his first term.

“Whoever does that job [has] big shoes to fill,” he said.

CNN reported Thursday that Trump has told his team he is not in a rush to decide on a replacement for Leavitt, who will depart her role at the end of the month.

Leavitt said Friday she will return to Trump’s MAGA Inc. super PAC after leaving the administration. She was a spokesperson for the group before joining the president’s 2024 campaign.

On Friday, Trump claimed he had “never seen so many job applications” for the press secretary role and complimented Jennings .

“Scott Jennings is good,” Trump told reporters at Joint Base Andrews in Maryland.

articles.title: Kyle Kirkwood wins IndyCar race in downtown D.C. celebrating U.S. 250th birthday
articles.summary: Reaching top speeds of about 180 mph, the cars zipped down Pennsylvania Ave between the Capitol and the White House.
articles.body: WASHINGTON — Blasting down these iconic and bumpy streets with a view of the U.S. Capitol from his car, Florida native Kyle Kirkwood took the checkered flag to win a once-in-a-lifetime IndyCar race on a sunny Sunday. The Freedom 250 Grand Prix was an elaborate 250-mile spectacle with few expenses spared to celebrate the country’s semiquincentennial, bringing the city a rare blend of power, money and speed. Kirkwood, who races for Andretti Global, started second but took the lead on the opening lap with a daring maneuver around the outside of pole-sitter and championship leader Alex Palou in front of the National Archives. From there he proved unbeatable. Reaching top speeds of about 180 mph during the weekend, the cars zipped down Pennsylvania Avenue between the Capitol and the White House, the longest straight on the track. They raced past the D.C. courthouse and the Smithsonian’s National Air and Space Museum on the seven-corner track. “You can’t even put it in words. This is incredible,” Kirkwood said in a postrace interview. “Man, that was a hard race. One hundred forty-seven laps. I’m out of breath right now.” President Donald Trump, who joined forces with D.C. Mayor Muriel Bowser to launch the race in January on short notice, waved the green flag to start the race. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy waved the checkered flag to end it. Trump sought to place himself at the center of the action, taking a “lap of honor” in the armored presidential limousine nicknamed “The Beast” ahead of the race and arranging an Air Force One flyover. It was one of seven waves of military flyovers in the preshow, capped with a pass from all six branches of the military with a B-2 bomber as the centerpiece. To hype the race, Trump hosted numerous events at the White House featuring IndyCar drivers and officials. He posed for a photo on the grid with first lady Melania Trump and several racers. After it became clear that Congress would reject an originally planned loop around the Capitol because of advertising restrictions on the grounds, Trump issued an executive order green-lighting the modified course. “We were going around the Capitol, but this turned out to be a better track — and so now we see the Capitol,” Trump told race broadcaster Fox Sports. “You see it right behind you. And I want everyone to be safe, and I want the people to have a good time.” The race also drew a long list of corporate sponsors, including Boeing, Starlink, Delta, Amazon and Shell. Several have major business interests before the federal government, putting some of the same companies seeking action from Washington front and center at the high-profile event. The race weekend featured two practice sessions Saturday, followed by qualifying in late afternoon to set the grid and a warmup Sunday before the Grand Prix. While officials have previewed the potential for it to become an annual spectacle, IndyCar has no plans to return to Washington for another race. Ahead of the race, drivers marveled at the spectacular views from inside their helmets. David Malukas told NBC News that seeing Washington’s iconic landmarks could pose a unique challenge for him and other drivers. “I think out of any track we’ve been to, this is the most distracting, especially coming out from that back straightaway. They’re leading into the Capitol building,” he said. Malukas crashed one turn later on Lap 37, bringing out the caution flag and causing most of the field to pit for fresh tires. Palou was given a drive-through penalty for a pit stop infringement, ending his hopes of victory. He later hit the wall and broke his front wing, falling to the back. Bowser estimated the attendance at 140,000 for each day of the weekend, selling the event as a way to showcase the city and boost the economy. But the road closures and other disruptions to the city irked plenty of locals, with some of the busiest streets shut down for the weekend, backing up traffic and forcing businesses to close. The federal courthouse canceled all hearings Friday ahead of the race, and flights in and out of National Airport were paused for several hours to accommodate the flyovers. Fans lined up behind the fence on Pennsylvania Avenue to get up close to the cars. One man wore a red “MAGA” hat and marveled at how clean the city was. Some wore Washington Nationals hats as D.C.-area locals, taking a short trip downtown for the spectacle. Others wore racing gear and merchandise for their favorite teams and drivers. “I love the racing. I love the cars,” said Luis Chavez of Maryland, a racing fan who showed up in a Pato O’Ward Arrow McLaren IndyCar shirt. He said he has watched NASCAR races, IndyCar races and even Formula 1 races in Brazil when he lived there. With three races left this season, Palou still leads the championship standings and remains favored to capture his fifth trophy. Kirkwood, who took a big chunk out of Palou’s lead in D.C., is still a distant second in the standings. Palou quipped that he’d like to win 10 more championships. “I’ve just been very blessed of being in the best team and having the best people around me,” he told NBC News before the race. “I don’t know if it’s going to end next year or in 10 years, but I’ll continue to push as much as I can.”

articles.title: Barrasso: Monday will be ‘D-Day for the economy in Iran’
articles.summary: Senate Majority Whip John Barrasso (R-Wyo.) said that Monday will be “D-Day” for the economy in Iran as the Trump administration and U.S. military vow to exert maximum financial and militaristic pressure on Tehran to end the war overseas. “Their economy is in shambles. And they’re still dangerous. So, the president’s right to focus on…
articles.body:
Senate Majority Whip John Barrasso (R-Wyo.) said that Monday will be “D-Day” for the economy in Iran as the Trump administration and U.S. military vow to exert maximum financial and militaristic pressure on Tehran to end the war overseas.

“Their economy is in shambles. And they’re still dangerous. So, the president’s right to focus on it. And now he’s going even further economically. And as you said, tomorrow is D-Day for the economy in Iran,” Barrasso told guest host Jason Chaffetz during a Sunday appearance on Fox News’s “ Sunday Morning Futures .”

The Wyoming senator said he believes the new pressure will cause the Iranian regime to fold — opening the Strait of Hormuz and agreeing to not having a nuclear weapon.

Iran’s decision to effectively close the Strait of Hormuz to commercial traffic ruptured the consistent flow of oil from the Middle East through a waterway responsible for carrying a fifth of the world’s oil transports daily.

The Trump administration’s primary component for an “economic D-Day” includes the aggressive use of secondary sanctions, meaning the U.S. will severely penalize any foreign nation, bank or business that acts as an economic lifeline to Iran.

Meanwhile, the Treasury Department has significantly ramped up enforcement on digital exchanges, freezing an estimated $500 billion in Iranian-linked cryptocurrency assets.

The U.S. Navy is also hunting down unregistered tankers and oil smuggling networks to drive Iranian crude exports to absolute zero while federal enforcement cracks down on alternative banking mechanisms, including currency swap lines, cash transfers and underground exchange houses, as reported by CBS .

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is scheduled to reveal the exact, detailed mechanics of the expanded Operation Economic Fury plan during a press conference on Monday.

On Sunday, Bessent said the impact of “economic D-Day” would be forceful.

“We are now entering the endgame. At dawn begins an economic D-Day — the single greatest financial offensive ever marshaled against an adversary. The Islamic Republic has subsisted by dressing extortion as security guarantees,” the Treasury Secretary wrote in a post on X.

“It has drawn strength from a calculus that regards Iranian retaliation as certain and American enforcement as negotiable. Under President Trump, that era is over. And those who fear the danger of defying Tehran ought not to discount the cost of testing Washington,” he added.

Despite efforts to ramp up punishment on Iran, their leaders say it’s a self-defeating mechanism that will only cause U.S. national debt to increase as the war drags on.

“The so-called ‘Economic D-Day’ is a diversion from America’s own crisis: unprecedented debt & surging interest costs,” Abbas Araghchi, the foreign minister of Iran, wrote on social media Thursday.

“Doubling down on failed policies will only bring further defeat—and enmity of Iranians,” he added.

articles.title: This week on the Hill: Georgia, South Carolina special elections draw focus
articles.summary: Lawmakers are fanning out across their districts and states for fundraisers, local events and campaign stops as the midterm elections heat up, while national party leaders are increasingly wading into races that could help shape control of Congress. In Georgia, voters are heading back to the polls Tuesday for a special election runoff to fill…
articles.body:
Lawmakers are fanning out across their districts and states for fundraisers, local events and campaign stops as the midterm elections heat up, while national party leaders are increasingly wading into races that could help shape control of Congress.

In Georgia, voters are heading back to the polls Tuesday for a special election runoff to fill the vacancy left by the death of longtime Rep. David Scott (D-Ga.), who died in April at age 80.

The runoff pits the late congressman’s daughter Marcye Scott (D) against Everton Blair Jr. (D), former Gwinnett County School Board chair. Marcye Scott garnered roughly 48 percent of the vote in the July primary, while Blair received about 35.6 percent, sending the two Democrats into Tuesday’s runoff, according to Decision Desk HQ .

The political spotlight will also turn to South Carolina, where Republicans are set for a closely watched Senate primary runoff between interim Sen. Darline Graham (R-S.C.) and Rep. Ralph Norman (R-S.C.).

Darline Graham — who was appointed to fill the seat belonging to her late brother, GOP Sen. Lindsey Graham (S.C.), and is running for a full term — has been in the spotlight in recent days after she said during a debate last week that she’s “not that informed on national security.”

And on the courts front, expect President Trump’s hush money conviction to be back in the spotlight. The judge mulling the president’s long-running bid to move his appeal out of New York’s state courts has newly indicated he expects to rule by Friday.

Trump wants to fight his conviction in federal court in the hopes of ultimately tossing it on presidential immunity grounds.

Democratic candidates vie in Georgia special election runoff: Marcye Scott, the late Rep. David Scott’s (D-Ga.) daughter; and Everton Blair Jr., former Gwinnett County School Board chair; will go head-to-head Tuesday.

President Trump backs Darline Graham: Trump is hoping to use his influence to convince GOP primary voters to choose Sen. Darline Graham over Rep. Ralph Norman in South Carolina’s Senate primary runoff.

Federal district judge to decide on hush money case: A federal judge will determine whether to move Trump’s appeal out of the New York state courts.

Georgia special election runoff puts late congressman’s daughter in focus

Marcye Scott previously told The Atlanta Journal-Constitution that she saw the special election to fill her late father’s seat as a way to carry on his legacy.

Rep. David Scott (D-Ga.) was first elected to Congress in 2002 and rose to prominence in 2021 when he became the first Black lawmaker to serve as chair of the House Agriculture Committee. He has been hailed by members of the Congressional Black Caucus, including House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-N.Y.), who characterized Scott as “a trailblazer” on Capitol Hill.

Georgia’s 13th Congressional District, a blue stronghold that David Scott had easily defended for decades, covers portions of six counties in the Atlanta metropolitan area.

The winner of the Aug. 25 runoff will represent the seat through the end of 2026.

Marcye Scott and Blair were two of three Democrats on the ballot in July, alongside former Judge Carlos Moore. Two Republicans also ran for the seat: Caesar Gonzales and Fayth Park. A fourth Democrat, Tony Brown, appeared on the ballot but had been disqualified.

Marcye Scott has been endorsed by Democratic Reps. Nikema Williams (Ga.) and Maxine Waters (Calif.), while Blair has been endorsed by Rep. Lucy McBath (D-Ga.).

Both candidates have centered their campaigns around affordability, a key issue in the midterms amid rising grocery prices, gas costs and inflation.

Blair wrote on social media that he launched his campaign because he believes in building a district “where housing is affordable, healthcare is accessible, schools are fully funded, and families aren’t stretched thin just trying to get by.”

Marcye Scott, meanwhile, has championed infrastructure investment, protection of veteran programs and benefit, and workforce development.

Graham, Norman go head-to-head in South Carolina runoff

Trump-backed Darline Graham is set to face off against Norman, who’s been endorsed by Rep. Nancy Mace (R-S.C.) and former South Carolina Gov. Mark Sanford (R), in the Senate primary runoff Tuesday.

Questions about whether Darline Graham is experienced enough to serve in the Senate roared to life after she flubbed a national security question. Norman told Kellie Meyer of NewsNation that Darline Graham’s debate response was “serious.”

But Darline Graham later told Fox News that, “I have said many times I’m not a politician, certainly not a career politician. I don’t speak politician.”

Trump stumped for Darline Graham in Myrtle Beach, which is home to former Senate candidate Rep. Russell Fry’s (R-S.C.) district. Fry did not advance out of the initial Republican primary election to replace Lindsey Graham, making his support base critical for both Norman and Darline Graham.

Graham has been backed by other prominent Republicans, including Sen. Tim Scott (S.C.) and the state’s lieutenant governor, Pamela Evette.

Sanford, meanwhile, endorsed Norman last week, arguing that “the stakes are simply too high as our nation really is at a financial tipping point.”

“I have seen first hand his experience in legislative circles, matched by a conservative voting record and conservative stands. And all of this brings me to a binary choice, not only on the bigger question of less government and more freedom, but on who do I believe holds the best shot at holding the line on government spending, our debt and its accompanying deficits? I am freaked about this issue given our crossing of the $40 trillion federal debt mark this week. It has heinous implications for all of us,” the former South Carolina governor wrote on social media.

Norman, a member of the House Freedom Caucus, wrote in a social media post that “the Senate has become a place where good legislation goes to die, and as we elect our next U.S. Senator, we NEED a PROVEN conservative to take up the mantle and fight!”

“I’m the only candidate in this race with the experience and the resume to take on this job, and I look forward to representing the Palmetto State in the United States Senate!” he added.

Trump hush money case in the spotlight again

U.S. District Judge Alvin Hellerstein indicated last week that he expects to issue a decision on whether to move Trump’s appeal in his hush money case out of the New York state courts.

Trump wants to move the case so he can try to convince a federal judge that the Supreme Court’s presidential immunity ruling compels tossing the jury’s 34-count guilty verdict.

Trump was convicted of falsifying business records in connection with a hush money scheme to keep quiet his alleged affair with porn actor Stormy Daniels ahead of the 2016 presidential election.

Trump has long argued he cannot get a fair shake in New York’s state court system and has repeatedly attacked the judge and jury that decided the case.

A three-judge panel on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 2nd Circuit ruled November last year that it “cannot be confident” a lower judge adequately considered Trump’s arguments as he sought to move the case.

“The court bypassed what we consider to be important issues bearing on the ultimate issue of good cause,” the panel wrote.

The panel emphasized it has no view on whether Trump’s strategy should ultimately succeed, only that the lower judge needs to reconsider his prior ruling.

“We leave it to the able and experienced District Judge to decide whether to solicit further briefing from the parties or hold a hearing to help it resolve these issues,” the panel wrote then.

articles.title: Pressure mounts on Ethics Committee to speed up misconduct probes as midterms loom
articles.summary: Democrats and Republicans are pressing the House Ethics Committee to move more quickly on investigations involving allegations of sexual misconduct or domestic abuse, as a string of high-profile cases and the looming midterms have renewed scrutiny of the secretive panel’s process. Investigations into Reps. Jimmy Gomez (D-Calif.), Cory Mills (R-Fla.) and Max Miller (R-Ohio) —…
articles.body:
Democrats and Republicans are pressing the House Ethics Committee to move more quickly on investigations involving allegations of sexual misconduct or domestic abuse, as a string of high-profile cases and the looming midterms have renewed scrutiny of the secretive panel’s process.

Investigations into Reps. Jimmy Gomez (D-Calif.), Cory Mills (R-Fla.) and Max Miller (R-Ohio) — involving allegations of sexual harassment, dating violence or domestic abuse — have dominated headlines in recent weeks, prompting lawmakers to argue that the Ethics Committee needs to find a way to expedite such cases.

The debate comes as two lawmakers known to be under investigation are seeking reelection, leaving the public in limbo over the status of the allegations against them and whether they will face any consequences before voting begins in the midterms.

“One of the long-standing problems of House Ethics investigations is that they simply take too long — staff, the public, and the Members need the investigations and reporting to be quicker and responsive,” Democratic Women’s Caucus Chair Rep. Teresa Leger Fernández (N.M.) said in a statement.

Leger Fernández — who has partnered with Rep. Kat Cammack (Fla.), chair of the Republican Women’s Caucus, to combat sexual misconduct on Capitol Hill — added, “Right now we’re talking with staff to finalize proposals that put staff voices and experiences first, but ultimately our work is about changing a culture that has allowed perpetrators to abuse their power without accountability.”

Rep. Anna Paulina Luna (R-Fla.) also argued on the social platform X earlier this month that there is a “massive problem with current Ethics Investigation process,” adding that “slow rolling investigations to protect party numbers is not due process. It is a cover up.”

The Ethics Committee announced Monday it was investigating allegations that Gomez violated House rules by “engaging in inappropriate sexual contact with a House staffer.” Gomez told The Hill in a previous statement his actions “were consensual in nature and haven’t violated the law or House Ethics rules.”

But two attorneys said Wednesday their client told the House Ethics Committee that Gomez sexually harassed and assaulted her.

The Democratic Women’s Caucus quickly called on the Ethics Committee to “release the status of their investigation, while protecting survivor privacy, before the 60-day blackout period ahead of Election Day.”

Gomez advanced from his primary in June and is set to face progressive Democrat Angela Gonzales-Torres in the general election.

Cammack said in a statement the committee “should move with urgency, and if these allegations are substantiated, Representative Gomez must resign and any criminal conduct must be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law.”

She added that the woman “showed real courage” in telling the committee about her experience and that she “deserves a process that is fast, fair, and fearless.”

“Due process must be respected, but it cannot be used to run out the clock,” she said.

Miller, who is facing Democratic opponent Brian Poindexter in November, has been in a similar hot seat . His ex-wife, Emily Moreno, has accused him of hurling hot water at her, pointing a gun at her head and breaking their daughter’s collarbone. Miller has denied the allegations and vowed not to drop his reelection bid.

The House Ethics Committee announced in early August that it was investigating Miller over domestic abuse and illegal drug use allegations.

The Ethics panel has also been investigating Mills since November 2025 over a wide swath of allegations, including whether he violated campaign finance laws, received special favors in his position, engaged in sexual misconduct, and misused congressional resources.

A state judge in October granted an ex-girlfriend of Mills a restraining order after she said he harassed her and threatened to release explicit images of her. Another woman Mills was dating initially told police he assaulted her in February 2025 before recanting. He has denied all allegations of wrongdoing.

Mills has previously faced calls to resign or be expelled. The Ethics investigation was still open when he lost his primary this month to Republican Ryan Elijah, a former news anchor for WOFL-TV in Orlando whom Luna and Rep. Mike Haridopolos (R-Fla.) both endorsed.

“Cory Mills is still in Congress a year and a half after criminal investigations [and] abuse, and we need real reform that’s going to ensure that members of Congress are actually held accountable,” Rep. Sam Liccardo (D-Calif.) told CNN earlier this month.

Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.) regularly points to the Ethics Committee when asked about allegations against lawmakers. In response to a question about Mills and Miller before the House left for its August recess, he told reporters the “key word there is allegation” and said to wait for the process to “shake out.”

Liccardo, however, told CNN that while he’s glad the investigation is happening, “the problem we’ve seen too often and the reason why Congress has been a safe haven for too many abusers is these investigations take far too long.”

Other lawmakers have resigned from Congress with probes into their conduct still pending, resulting in the committee ending the investigations.

Former Reps. Tony Gonzales (R-Texas) and Eric Swalwell (D-Calif.), who had both been accused of sexual misconduct, were under investigation when pressure to resign from lawmakers on both sides of the aisle contributed to their departure from Congress in April.

Rep. Chuck Edwards (R-N.C.), on the other hand, dropped his reelection bid this month after the House Ethics Committee recommended that he be formally censured following an investigation that found he violated the “spirit” of the chamber’s policies on sexual harassment against staff. Cammack said in a statement that the House should follow through with the censure.

The Hill has reached out to the Ethics Committee’s leadership for comment.

House Ethics Committee Chair Michael Guest (R-Miss.) told Bloomberg News back in April that the committee would be “receptive” to changes that would expedite investigations.

“If leadership wishes to change the Ethics process and the fact of additional resources, additional jurisdiction, I think that is a decision for the Speaker and the minority leader to make in conjunction with one another,” Guest said at the time.

articles.title: Reform says it will prioritise British-born young workers for social housing
articles.summary: Labour called the plan "unserious and unworkable" and accused Reform of pushing "gimmicks and division".
articles.body:
Reform UK has said it will prioritise British-born workers under 35 when allocating social housing if it were to enter government.

On top of British-born workers, former military service personnel and married couples with children will also be prioritised, Reform said.

A Labour spokesperson called the plans "unserious and unworkable", saying it could leave British citizens without a home.

Deputy leader Richard Tice has also set out plans to build 50,000 affordable social homes a year at a news conference, a policy which the party says will require no new taxes or borrowing.

Farage vows to ban foreign nationals from social housing Published 15 June

Farage vows to ban foreign nationals from social housing

Reform plans to scrap indefinite leave to remain for migrants Published 22 September 2025

Reform plans to scrap indefinite leave to remain for migrants

Tice said he wanted the rules on who was allocated a home to be changed away from need to suitability, putting British families, workers and veterans at the front of the queue, saying: "This comes down to fairness."

"We're saying that the first people we should be looking after are young, British workers - under 35, young British married couples, young British veterans - who have done the right thing," he said.

"They've got a job, they're doing their best, working in their community, setting a fine example, because the role of the British government is actually to look after British citizens first."

Rules would be changed to reserve at least half of all social homes in England for British-born workers aged under 35, with prioritisation also given to married couples, veterans, victims of domestic violence and care leavers.

Tice claimed there were currently 540,000 existing affordable social homes occupied by overseas nationals and he wanted that to change.

"It's not fair that young British working families can't get on the housing ladder when overseas nationals have come to the UK and, because of the current rules based on need rather than suitability, they have jumped ahead in the queue," he said.

"We just don't think that's right: I can't think of another country where you rock up with a family and you expect the local taxpayer in that country to pay for your housing needs."

UK or Irish nationals made up 88.5% of main social home householders in 2024/25, according to the English Housing Survey.

That means around 11.5% of main householders, the per­son in whose name the social home is ren­ted, were non-UK or Irish nation­als.

For its part, Reform estimates 540,000 social homes are currently occupied by foreign nationals.

Reform has previously announced it would evict foreign nationals from social housing - a plan criticised by housing charity Shelter which said building more homes is the solution, rather than "changing the order of the queue" and "stoking division".

Tice also said Reform would raise £10bn a year to build new homes, in part by reintroducing the Right to Buy scheme of the 1980s, allowing people to buy council homes at a discount.

"The failure then was they didn't reinvest the proceeds into building more affordable homes," he said, adding he believed reinvestment would raise a third of the investment needed to build 50,000 homes a year over a decade.

Tice said another third would be raised via housing authorities, and the final third would be money from local government pension schemes.

A Labour Party spokesperson said the plan was "unworkable and unserious", adding: "It would blow a £10bn blackhole in the public finances, would create years of wrangling with the EU, and could leave British citizens without a place to call home.

"This Labour government is investing billions to deliver the biggest boost to social and affordable housing in a generation, to fix the housing crisis we inherited from the Tories."

The Conservative Party, which also said it would revoke the right of foreign nationals to social housing, accused Reform of "trying to catch up" with its policies.

The Tories have said their plan, which would allow Irish citizens and some EU nationals to remain in social housing, would free up around 230,000 homes.

Sir James Cleverly, shadow housing secretary, added: "The Conservatives have already set out comprehensive plans to ensure British nationals are at the front of the queue for social housing. Now Reform are trying to catch up.

"We also believe in a home owning society and that those who work hard should be able to buy their own home, without unnecessary barriers standing in their way."

Liberal Democrat spokesperson Gideon Amos said that Reform's plan was a "cruel gimmick".

Green MP Siân Berry said her party would tackle housing issues by ending Right to Buy, building and buying hundreds of thousands of new council homes, and introducing rent controls.

She added: "Another blatantly racist and cruel policy from Reform, adding to a host of plans to create a two-tier Britain – one for those born in the UK and one for everyone else."

articles.title: Sullivan endorses Sullivan against Sullivan in Alaska
articles.summary: Three Dan Sullivans are wading in on Alaska’s Senate race but only one Dan Sullivan has earned the support of a former lawmaker with his namesake. Sen. Dan S. articles.body:
Three Dan Sullivans are wading in on Alaska’s Senate race but only one Dan Sullivan has earned the support of a former lawmaker with his namesake.

Sen. Dan S. Sullivan (R-Alaska) was endorsed by former Anchorage Mayor Dan A. Sullivan (R) last Tuesday as he prepares to face off against Dan J. Sullivan and Rep. Mary Peltola (D-Alaska) in November.

“As the OG Dan Sullivan, I urge Alaskans to vote for Sen. Daniel S. Sullivan. He’s been great for Alaska,” the former mayor of Anchorage wrote in a Facebook post last week.

The post comes after Dan J. Sullivan’s campaign faced legal challenges , as Dan S. Sullivan and the National Republican Senatorial Committee accused him of launching a Senate bid to create confusion for voters seeking to elect the incumbent lawmaker.

Carol Beecher, a registered Republican and the director of the Alaska Division of Elections, attempted to remove Dan J. Sullivan from the primary ballot and disqualify his campaign, citing his logo’s similarities to the incumbent senator’s.

However, Dan J. Sullivan challenged the measure in court, and in June, Superior Court Judge Thomas Matthews ruled that Dan J. Sullivan could remain on the ballot for the state’s primary on Aug. 18.

Republicans Dan J. Sullivan and Dan S. Sullivan advanced to Alaska’s general nonpartisan election in November alongside Democrat Peltola (Alaska), who Dan. J. Sullivan has said he voted for twice in previous elections.

The race is considered a toss-up by the nonpartisan Cook Political Report while Decision Desk HQ has Peltola favored to win due to her past success in statewide races and status as a moderate Democrat who hires Republican staffers on the Hill.

Some Republicans have accused Dan J. Sullivan of being a Democratic plant and entering the race to siphon votes away from the incumbent senator with the same name.

Dan J. Sullivan, a retired teacher, has denied those accusations.

articles.title: Bernie Moreno says Natalie Harp discourse has been ‘super misogynistic’
articles.summary: Sen. Bernie Moreno (R-Ohio) on Sunday said discussions regarding White House aide Natalie Harp in recent days have been “super misogynistic.” Democrats and former White House staffers have said Harp’s relationship with President Trump has been inappropriate, citing reporting from The Daily Beast that unveiled letters to Trump in which she professes her allegiance to…
articles.body:
Sen. Bernie Moreno (R-Ohio) on Sunday said discussions regarding White House aide Natalie Harp in recent days have been “super misogynistic.”

Democrats and former White House staffers have said Harp’s relationship with President Trump has been inappropriate, citing reporting from The Daily Beast that unveiled letters to Trump in which she professes her allegiance to him.

“You are all that matters to me,” Harp wrote to Trump in one letter. “I don’t want to ever let you down.”

In a separate letter, she wrote, “And please, when I fail, will you tell me? You have the absolute right to cuss me out, if need be, when I deserve it, because no one knows or cares about me more.”

In response to comments alleging an inappropriate relationship between Harp and the president, Moreno told reporters , “That’s super misogynistic.”

“I mean, the reality is she’s a very talented person. She’s very smart at what she does. She helps the president make sure he’s communicating. And the fact that if it was a guy, nobody would say that,” he added.

Moreno said rumors are arising because Harp is “a woman” and “obviously … pretty.”

“When the reality is she’s very talented, she’s very, very smart. I happen to know her very well. It’s also obviously a very kind person. She went through bone cancer in her 20s,” Moreno said.

“I mean, look at the other day, I’ve always said, let’s just keep personal issues out,” he added.

Harp is affectionately referred to as the “human printer” in the White House and is often seen at Trump’s side on Air Force One flights and high-level meetings to provide news clippings and comments for the president on demand.

She campaigned for him in 2024 after she credited Trump for saving her life by signing the Right to Try Act, which gave her access to medical treatments that cured her of cancer.

Following the campaign, Harp transitioned from a television host on One America News Network to a key West Wing aide and executive assistant to the president.

Sen. Jon Ossoff (D-Ga.) recently said Trump “doesn’t want to do the job” of president and would rather focus on the White House ballroom project and “travel with Natalie on their apparently defenseless flying palace gifted by the Emir of Qatar.” Ossoff made the comments during a campaign rally two weeks ago, referring to the newer Air Force One jet , causing pushback from the White House.

Eric Trump also stepped in to defend Harp , writing, “Natalie is an incredible young woman — a cancer survivor, a genuinely good person, and arguably one of the hardest-working people in the White House. She’s deeply committed to my father, to her job, and to this country,” in a post on the social platform X.

articles.title: Nova Zelândia quer proibir redes sociais para menores de 16 anos | G1
articles.standfirst: Proposta prevê multas de até 10% da receita global das plataformas; medida enfrenta resistência de um dos partidos da coalizão de governo.
articles.summary: Proposta prevê multas de até 10% da receita global das plataformas; medida enfrenta resistência de um dos partidos da coalizão de governo.
articles.body:
Jovem usa o celular em Sidney, na Austrália; país aprovou lei que proíbe acesso de menores de 16 anos às redes sociais — Foto: Hollie Adams/Reuters

O primeiro-ministro da Nova Zelândia, Christopher Luxon, disse nesta segunda-feira (24) que seu partido apresentará ao Parlamento um projeto de lei para proibir crianças menores de 16 anos de usar redes sociais.

A proposta prevê multas de até 10% da receita global das plataformas que não cumprirem a medida.

🗒️ Tem alguma sugestão de reportagem? Mande para o g1

O texto exigiria que as empresas adotassem medidas razoáveis para verificar a idade dos usuários, incluindo o uso de informações de contas existentes, tecnologia de reconhecimento facial e documentos de identidade digital.

"Simplesmente não podemos aceitar o mal que está sendo causado a uma geração de crianças neozelandesas", disse Luxon em um comunicado.

"As redes sociais estão expondo-as a conteúdo prejudicial, tecnologias viciantes e pressões para as quais não estão preparadas. Isso está afetando sua vida familiar, saúde mental, sono e educação", afirmou.

Ainda não está claro se o projeto terá apoio suficiente para ser aprovado pelo Parlamento. Um dos partidos que integram a coalizão de governo de Luxon, o Nova Zelândia Primeiro, já afirmou que não apoiará a proposta.

"Estamos preocupados com a legislação proposta e com a direção e o caminho perigoso que uma medida como essa inevitavelmente levará nosso país", disse Winston Peters, líder do partido e ministro das Relações Exteriores, em uma publicação no X.

Em dezembro, a Austrália se tornou o primeiro país do mundo a proibir o uso de redes sociais por menores de 16 anos . A medida restringe o acesso a plataformas como TikTok, YouTube, Instagram e Facebook.

A legislação australiana foi um "fracasso colossal", disse Peters. Segundo ele, manter as crianças longe das redes sociais deveria ser responsabilidade dos pais.

"Não vou fingir que será simples ou que será perfeito", disse Luxon em um evento.

"Não vamos conseguir tirar todas as crianças das redes sociais. Algumas sempre encontrarão maneiras de contornar isso, mas, francamente, é importante demais para não tentarmos", afirmou.

articles.title: Eleições 2026: ministro da Fazenda defende combater 'pejotização' para conter déficit da Previdência Social | G1
articles.standfirst: Durigan falou novamente como representante da campanha à reeleição do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, que busca um quarto mandato. Segundo ele, há estudos que mostram que algumas empresas tiveram uma migração de empregados celetistas para pessoa jurídica.
articles.summary: Durigan falou novamente como representante da campanha à reeleição do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, que busca um quarto mandato. Segundo ele, há estudos que mostram que algumas empresas tiveram uma migração de empregados celetistas para pessoa jurídica.
articles.body:
O ministro da Fazenda, Dario Durigan, defendeu nesta segunda-feira (24) o combate à chamada "pejotização" como forma de combater o crescente rombo na Previdência Social.

🔎 A "pejotização" é uma contratação sistemática de trabalhadores como pessoas jurídicas (PJ), e não como empregados com carteira assinada. O modelo é legal em diversas atividades, mas gera controvérsia quando é usado para substituir vínculos formais de trabalho previstos na legislação trabalhista.

Em entrevista à Broadcast, da Agência Estado, Durigan falou novamente como representante da campanha à reeleição do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) — que busca um quarto mandato.

De acordo com o ministro, há estudos que mostram que algumas empresas tiveram uma migração de empregados celetistas para "pejotizados", o que estaria gerando uma piora no déficit da Previdência Social.

Esses empregados podem, por exemplo, estar sendo contratados como microempreendedores, que têm contribuição reduzida.

"Poderia se ter uma regra no país de uma porcentagem do que uma empresa contrata como pejotizado ou não. Se tem 10% [contratado como pejotizado], está terceirizando um serviço e que é da regra do jogo, é ok. Agora uma empresa que tem 80% da sua força de trabalho pejotizada, eventualmente pode ter de obrigar essa empresa a ter uma contribuição previdenciária para nivelar e poder oferecer aos seus trabalhadores um futuro um pouco mais protegido do ponto de vista da seguridade social", explicou o ministro Durigan.

Ele afirmou que esse tipo de regra tem sido estudada pela equipe econômica, e pode ser apresentada ao Congresso Nacional em um novo mandato do presidente Lula.

"A gente já fez alguns debates nesse sentido", acrescentou o ministro da Fazenda.

Esse tema já havia sido comentado também pelo ministro do Trabalho, Luiz Marinho. No fim de junho, ele disse que o MEI não pode ser utilizado para fraudes trabalhistas e que o micrompreendedor não pode ter características de trabalhadores com carteira assinada.

Na ocasião, o ministro afirmou que há situações em que isso aconteceria – ele cita como exemplo o caso de um hospital que fizesse uma licitação para terceirização de alguma atividade e a empresa terceirizada contratasse MEIs como funcionários formais.

Segundo o ministro, isso poderia "arrebentar" recursos como com a Previdência, o Fundo de Garantia por Tempo de Serviço (FGTS) e o Sistema S, que reúne instituições como Senai, Sesi e Senac.

Marinho disse esperar que o Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), que julga ação sobre pejotização na economia , não permita que isso aconteça.

"Não podemos é utilizar o MEI como uma fraude trabalhista, precisa ser empreendedor. Não é o enfermeiro, não é o gari. Isso é fraude trabalhista, não é o gerente. O conceito de debate do que é PJ e não precisa ficar claro, o Supremo tem a responsabilidade de não cometer a irresponsabilidade de permitir contratar PJ como empreendedor. Tem que caracterizar o que é empreendedor", disse Marinho a jornalistas, em junho.

Ministro da Fazenda, Dario Durigan — Foto: Washington Costa/MF

articles.title: Ancine concede registro a 'Dark Horse', cinebiografia de Jair Bolsonaro | G1
articles.standfirst: Concessão do Registro de Obra Estrangeira (ROE) é etapa preliminar ao registro definitivo da obra. Em paralelo, agência apura irregularidade na gravação do filme.
articles.summary: Concessão do Registro de Obra Estrangeira (ROE) é etapa preliminar ao registro definitivo da obra. Em paralelo, agência apura irregularidade na gravação do filme.
articles.body:
A Agência Nacional do Cinema (Ancine) concedeu o Registro de Obra Estrangeira (ROE) de Dark Horse, filme sobre a trajetória do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro (PL).

O pedido, aceito no dia 7 de agosto, é uma etapa preliminar ao registro definitivo da obra ( veja os próximos passos abaixo ).

🎥O filme "Dark Horse" ganhou notoriedade após a divulgação, pelo site Intercept Brasil, de conversas entre o pré-candidato do PL à Presidência, Flávio Bolsonaro, e o ex-banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro, do banco Master, em que o filho de Jair solicita recursos para financiar a produção cinematográfica.

O filme, protagonizado pelo ator norte-americano Jim Caviezel no papel de Jair Bolsonaro, terá 1h40 de duração e é classificada pela Ancine como uma obra de ficção.

A concessão do registro ocorre ao mesmo tempo que a Ancine abriu um processo administrativo contra a produtora responsável pelo filme, a Go Up Entertainment .

O processo foi aberto após uma denúncia sobre a gravação, em território brasileiro, de uma obra audiovisual estrangeira sem comunicação prévia à agência.

Pela regulamentação, produções estrangeiras filmadas no Brasil precisam informar previamente a Ancine e apresentar documentos sobre a produção.

Além disso, na semana passada, a Polícia Federal solicitou à Ancine informações sobre o processo aberto contra o filme . Segundo a Ancine, a Go Up não havia apresentado a documentação exigida para as gravações.

A empresa pode ser multada em R$ 2 mil a R$ 100 mil caso a irregularidade seja confirmada.

Jim Caviezel no pôster de 'Dark Horse' — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram/therealjimcaviezel

O pedido da PF ocorre em paralelo à investigação sobre o financiamento do filme. O Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) autorizou, em julho deste ano, a abertura de um inquérito para apurar os repasses feitos pelo empresário Daniel Vorcaro, ex-controlador do Banco Master, para a produção.

A investigação busca verificar se os recursos foram efetivamente utilizados para financiar Dark Horse.

LEIA TAMBÉM: 'Dark Horse': entenda o que a PF vai investigar sobre a cinebiografia de Jair Bolsonaro

A origem do caso está em mensagens e áudios que indicam que o candidato à Presidência, Flávio Bolsonaro (PF), teria pedido dinheiro a Vorcaro para financiar o filme.

O valor inicialmente mencionado nas negociações chegou a US$ 24 milhões (cerca de R$ 134 milhões), embora os valores efetivamente transferidos sejam objeto da investigação.

Após obter o registro, o responsável pela obra deverá solicitar o Certificado de Registro de Título (CRT), indicando o segmento de mercado em que a obra será explorada.

No caso de um filme destinado à exibição comercial em cinemas, como é o de "Dark Horse", o segmento correspondente é o de salas de exibição.

Para a emissão do CRT, deve ser demonstrada a detenção dos direitos de exploração comercial da obra no Brasil e para o segmento pretendido, mediante a apresentação do contrato de cessão, licenciamento ou transferência desses direitos.

Registro de Obra Estrangeira (ROE) de "Dark Horse", filme sobre Jair Bolsonaro — Foto: Reprodução

Quando houver uma cadeia de contratos, como nos casos que envolvem produtor estrangeiro, agente internacional de vendas e distribuidor brasileiro, a documentação deve permitir verificar a transferência dos direitos até o responsável pela exploração comercial no Brasil.

O certificado, portanto, está vinculado à etapa de exploração comercial da obra e não representa uma exigência para a realização das filmagens.

A conclusão do procedimento de registro depende do atendimento das eventuais exigências e diligências formuladas pela Ancine. Os procedimentos regulamentares de registro têm prazo de até 30 dias para conclusão quando não houver exigências a serem cumpridas.

Após a emissão do CRT é necessário ainda a obtenção da classificação indicativa no Ministério da Justiça, para depois lançar comercialmente o filme nas salas de cinema.

A obra só poderá ser lançada comercialmente após o cumprimento de todas as etapas.

articles.summary: Pesquisa divulgada nesta segunda-feira (24) foi encomendada pela Inter TV Cabugi. Na pesquisa espontânea, em que os nomes dos pré-candidatos não são mostrados aos eleitores, 78% estão indecisos.
articles.body:
Pesquisa Quaest divulgada nesta segunda-feira (24) mostra como está a disputa pelo Senado no Rio Grande do Norte. O levantamento foi encomendado pela Inter TV Cabugi.

Em 2026, serão eleitos dois senadores em cada estado e no Distrito Federal, para renovar 54 das 81 cadeiras. Por isso, cada eleitor precisa votar em dois candidatos diferentes. Não é possível escolher o mesmo nome duas vezes.

Na pesquisa espontânea da Quaest — em que os nomes não são mostrados aos eleitores entrevistados —, 78% estão indecisos, porque não souberam citar um candidato.

Já na pesquisa estimulada, a lista de candidatos é mostrada, e cada entrevistado precisa responder duas vezes em quem pretende votar: para a primeira vaga e, depois, para a segunda vaga.

Os resultados da pesquisa para o Senado consideram as menções para a primeira e a segunda vagas em um total que soma 100% das intenções de voto e mantém a proporção entre candidatos, brancos/nulos e indecisos. Veja os números abaixo:

Agora, veja os resultados que consideram apenas as respostas para a primeira vaga e, depois, para a segunda.

Para 61% dos eleitores ouvidos no levantamento, a escolha do candidato é definitiva. Outros 39% dizem que ainda podem mudar o voto até as eleições, em 4 de outubro.

A Quaest ouviu 804 pessoas de 16 anos ou mais entre os dias 20 e 23 de agosto. A margem de erro é de 3 pontos percentuais, para mais ou para menos, e o nível de confiança é de 95%. O número de registro no TSE é RN-00876/2026.

Abaixo, veja os dados completos da pesquisa espontânea.

A Quaest perguntou também aos eleitores sobre cada um dos candidatos: se eles conhecem e votariam, se não conhecem ou se conhecem e não votariam. Os candidatos mais rejeitados (maiores índices de "conhece e não votaria") são Sandro Pimentel (PSOL) e Zenaide Maia (PSD).

articles.summary: Em entrevista à Globo, o candidato Romeu Zema vinculou o reajuste do salário mínimo ao crescimento econômico e comentou possíveis mudanças na Previdência.
articles.body:
O candidato do Novo à Presidência da República, Romeu Zema, afirmou nesta segunda-feira (24), em entrevista à Globo, que, se eleito, garantirá a reposição da inflação no salário mínimo, mas não se comprometeu com aumento real. Segundo ele, reajustes acima da inflação dependerão do desempenho da economia.

O ex-governador ainda disse que manteria o ganho com relação ao crescimento dos dois anos anteriores se a economia “estiver indo bem”.

Zema propõe ajuste fiscal para baixar juros a 6%, sem detalhar medidas, e defende anistia para condenados do 8 de janeiro

Zema disse que a prioridade dele, se eleito, é que a taxa de juros caia. “Com um governo sério, com credibilidade, combatendo corrupção e fraudes, essa taxa cai para 6%. Só aí nós vamos ter uma economia de R$ 800 bilhões por ano”.

Zema afirmou ainda que, “por ora”, não pretende aumentar as idades mínimas para aposentadoria. O candidato, porém, não descartou mudanças futuras e disse que eventuais alterações nas regras da Previdência dependerão de fatores como o aumento da expectativa de vida da população e uma maior formalização do mercado de trabalho.

Questionado sobre possíveis mudanças nas regras para trabalhadores rurais e militares, Zema também condicionou decisões ao resultado do ajuste fiscal que pretende implementar caso seja eleito.

Segundo o candidato, medidas para reduzir gastos, combater fraudes e corrupção e tornar a administração pública mais eficiente podem diminuir a necessidade de novas alterações nas regras previdenciárias.

"A aposentadoria vai depender muito disso. Agora, o brasileiro já trabalha muito. Eu não quero o brasileiro trabalhando mais. Eu quero a renda do brasileiro aumentando”, afirmou Zema.

Os candidatos ao governo do Maranhão cumpriram agendas de campanha nesta segunda-feira (24) e apresentaram propostas voltadas para a agricultura, agricultura familiar e o agronegócio.

Felipe Camarão (PT), Eduardo Braide (PSD), Saulo Arcangeli (PSTU) e Roberto Rocha (PRTB) participaram de reuniões, entrevistas e encontros com apoiadores em diferentes regiões do estado.

Saiba como foi a agenda do candidato Saulo Arcangeli:

Saulo Arcangeli realizou agenda no Terminal da Praia Grande, no Centro de São Luís. O candidato conversou com eleitores, apresentou propostas e esteve acompanhado da equipe de campanha e de candidatos da chapa.

Na área rural, Arcangeli afirmou que pretende combater a ocupação irregular de terras públicas e restringir o uso de agrotóxicos na agricultura familiar.O candidato também defendeu ampliar o acesso à terra, ao crédito e aos mercados consumidores para pequenos produtores.

articles.title: Discord recorre de suspensão de lives e diz que ANPD aplicou punição 'desproporcional' à plataforma | G1
articles.standfirst: Autoridade Nacional de Proteção de Dados suspendeu transmissões da plataforma até que o Discord comprove que adotou medidas para proteger menores. Em julho, adolescente se suicidou durante live.
articles.summary: Autoridade Nacional de Proteção de Dados suspendeu transmissões da plataforma até que o Discord comprove que adotou medidas para proteger menores. Em julho, adolescente se suicidou durante live.
articles.body:
O Discord apresentou nesta segunda-feira (24) um recurso contra a suspensão de lives da plataforma determinada pela Autoridade Nacional de Proteção de Dados (ANPD).

A empresa solicita efeito suspensivo imediato com o objetivo de reativar as transmissões e pede a anulação da medida cautelar, alegando falta de competência da agência para aplicar a restrição, vícios formais no processo e punição "desproporcional".

🔎 O debate sobre a segurança no ambiente digital ganhou força nas últimas semanas após a primeira-dama, Janja da Silva, dizer que o Discord deveria ser retirado do ar “imediatamente” , ao se referir a uma adolescente que tirou a própria vida durante transmissões em grupos da plataforma .

💻 O Discord é uma plataforma de comunicação bastante utilizada por jogadores de games online e também por adolescentes. A empresa tem sido alvo de críticas e investigações relacionadas a falhas na moderação de conteúdo e na verificação da idade dos usuários.

A ordem de suspensão atingiu a ferramenta "Go Live" e recursos equivalentes de transmissão e compartilhamento de vídeo. A determinação foi cumprida pelo Discord em 17 de agosto .

🔎 A ANPD é uma agência reguladora vinculada ao Ministério da Justiça , cuja missão é zelar pela proteção de dados pessoais.

Segundo a ANPD, a suspensão valerá até que o Discord comprove que adotou medidas efetivas para proteger crianças e adolescentes durante o uso da plataforma.

Punição atinge quem não tem elo com ilícitos, diz defesa

No recurso protocolado, a plataforma diz que a ANPD não tem competência legal para determinar a suspensão de serviços sob o marco do ECA Digital.

A defesa do Discord afirma que a lei estabelece que sanções como advertência e multa cabem à autoridade administrativa, mas a suspensão temporária ou proibição de atividades é atribuição da justiça.

A defesa também declara que, mesmo dentro da esfera administrativa, uma medida de tamanho impacto e alcance nacional não poderia ter sido emitida monocraticamente pelo Superintendente de Fiscalização.

O recurso do Discord afirma ainda que o bloqueio das chamadas de vídeo em grupo e transmissões privadas afeta diariamente famílias, estudantes, comunidades e empresas em todo o Brasil que nada têm a ver com condutas ilícitas.

Caso a suspensão das lives não seja integralmente anulada ou reconsiderada pela Superintendência, o Discord pede o envio do processo ao Conselho Diretor da ANPD.

A conversão da suspensão em um Plano de Conformidade, com cronograma técnico de entregas e metas claras;

A fixação imediata de prazo e critérios objetivos para a reativação faseada dos serviços;

O prosseguimento das discussões institucionais e a formalização de um Termo de Ajustamento de Conduta (TAC) centralizado na autoridade.

Depois de live que terminou em morte, Discord suspende transmissões ao vivo no país — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

articles.title: Romeu Zema (Novo), candidato à Presidência, concede entrevista à Globo | G1
articles.standfirst: Os jornalistas Renata Vasconcellos e César Tralli conduziram a primeira entrevista da série da Globo com os candidatos à Presidência da República, direto dos Estúdios Globo, no Rio de Janeiro.
articles.summary: Romeu Zema abre a rodada de conversas com presidenciáveis sob o comando de Renata Vasconcellos e César Tralli, com transmissão ao vivo no g1 e GloboNews.
articles.body:
O candidato do Novo à Presidência da República, Romeu Zema , afirmou nesta segunda-feira (24) que, se eleito, vai promover medidas de ajuste fiscal para que a taxa básica de juros, a Selic, caia a 6% ao ano. Atualmente, a Selic está em 14% ao ano .

LEIA TAMBÉM: Zema não garante aumento real do salário mínimo e diz que, 'por ora', não mexeria em idades de aposentadoria

Zema não detalhou, no entanto, em que consistiria esse ajuste fiscal ou como faria para obter a redução na taxa de juros.

O candidato disse ainda que, se eleito, vai garantir que o salário mínimo seja reajustado pela inflação. “Garanto que ninguém vai ter perda”, disse o ex-governador de Minas Gerais. Um reajuste com ganho real, porém, estaria condicionado ao bom desempenho da economia, disse.

LEIA TAMBÉM: Veja o que é #FATO e o que é #FAKE na entrevista de Romeu Zema à Globo

Zema concedeu nesta segunda-feira (24) entrevista à Globo. A atração foi exibida ao vivo dos Estúdios Globo, no Rio de Janeiro, com transmissão pelo g1 e pela GloboNews. Ao longo desta semana, até sábado, serão entrevistados os candidatos Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), Renan Santos (Missão), Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e Augusto Cury (Avante).

Romeu Zema, candidato à Presidência da República pelo Novo — Foto: Globo/ Manoella Mello

Veja destaques da entrevista de Romeu Zema à Globo:

Ao falar sobre propostas de ajuste fiscal, Zema disse que, se eleito, garantirá a reposição da inflação no salário mínimo.

“Garanto que ninguém vai ter perda”, declarou. “Se tiver inflação, nós daremos toda a inflação. É um absurdo um aposentado não ter a reposição inflacionária ou, pior, ficar sem receber a aposentadoria”.

O ex-governador ainda disse que manteria o ganho com relação ao crescimento dos dois anos anteriores se a economia “estiver indo bem”.

Zema disse que a prioridade dele, se eleito, é que a taxa de juros caia. “Com um governo sério, com credibilidade, combatendo corrupção e fraudes, essa taxa cai para 6%. Só aí nós vamos ter uma economia de R$ 800 bilhões por ano”.

A primeira pergunta a Zema foi sobre como ele pretende, se eleito, equilibrar os gastos do país, dado que, enquanto governador de Minas Gerais, a dívida pública do estado praticamente dobrou. Segundo ele, isso aconteceu porque o déficit foi “herdado dos anos 90” e porque o governo federal cobrava juros altos.

Zema afirmou que não fez nenhum empréstimo ou financiamento durante sua gestão de quase 8 anos em Minas.

“Eu paguei R$ 23 bilhões para aposentado que não recebia aposentadoria”, disse. “Eu paguei R$ 13 bilhões para o governo federal, funcionários públicos, e hoje a dívida representa muito menos para a economia de Minas do que representava quando eu assumi.”

Ainda de acordo com o candidato, ele assumiu com um déficit de R$ 11 bilhões em 2018 e deixou o cargo com um superávit de R$ 5 bilhões. “Ou seja, o estado gastando menos do que arrecada, e antes gastava-se muito mais do que arrecadava. O ajuste foi feito.”

Zema foi questionado sobre seu posicionamento contrário à vacinação obrigatória de crianças. O Estado de São Paulo enfrenta um surto de sarampo. O candidato concorda que situações como esta colocam em risco a sociedade como um todo.

“Eu tomei todas as vacinas da Covid, acredito na ciência, recomendo que tome. Em Minas, eu recomendei que as crianças tomassem”, disse. “Agora, eu não posso permitir que uma família, uma criança seja perseguida porque alguém não tomou a vacina."

Para o candidato, o papel do governo é fazer campanha de conscientização e vacinar o maior número de pessoas possível. Segundo ele, a obrigatoriedade não pode ser imposta em “um país democrático”.

O candidato disse que, se eleito presidente, dará anistia aos condenados pelos atos golpistas de 8 de janeiro de 2023 e classificou o julgamento dessas pessoas, feito pelo STF, como “nitidamente político”.

Segundo Zema, os responsáveis devem ser punidos por vandalismo e depredação. Na avaliação dele, há tribunais no Brasil “fazendo mais política do que propriamente justiça”.

“Eu darei anistia ou, pelo menos, no mínimo, um tribunal que não seja político, um tribunal que seja judicial”, disse.

Zema também afirmou confiar nas urnas eletrônicas, embora defenda que o sistema poderia ser “melhorado” com voto impresso.

"Vale lembrar: eu sou totalmente democrata, fui eleito pela urna eletrônica, confio na urna eletrônica — que poderia ser melhorada se tivesse impresso, mas confio."

Zema afirmou que medidas adotadas pelo governo de Nayib Bukele, presidente de El Salvador, para reduzir os homicídios podem ser adaptadas ao Brasil. O candidato visitou o país em maio de 2025 para conhecer a política de segurança pública.

Questionado especificamente sobre medidas do governo Bukele, como suspensão de direitos, Zema disse que não concorda, mas disse que o exemplo salvadorenho o inspira por ter colocado criminosos “atrás das grades” e reduzido os homicídios. “Será que não é isso que nós queremos aqui? Nós podemos fazer prisões aqui dentro da nossa lei”, afirmou.

Questionado sobre como combateria a violência contra as mulheres, o candidato citou a ampliação do número de delegacias especializadas no atendimento à mulher, com atendimento feito por funcionárias femininas, e de casas de acolhimento para vítimas de violência doméstica.

Também mencionou o uso de recursos tecnológicos, como tornozeleiras eletrônicas com distância mínima de 200 metros da vítima e possibilidade de chamar automaticamente a polícia. Disse, ainda, que o aspecto mais importante é a conscientização nas escolas. “Toda criança deve ser conscientizada de que, caso tenha violência em casa, precisa considerar isso anormal”.

Em seguida, Zema foi questionado sobre o aumento do número de feminicídios registrados em Minas Gerais em 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023 e 2025, durante o governo dele.

“Quando eu assumi, eu sempre pego a estatística antes do meu governo e no meu governo. E eu posso te assegurar que nós reduzimos. Algum repique sempre pode acontecer”, respondeu. “Agora, o que vale é a tendência ao longo do tempo. Mas todas as medidas, todos esses planos foram feitos em Minas. Vale lembrar, tem uma taxa menor do que a média.”

Ao ser questionado sobre a promessa de privatizar estatais federais se for eleito presidente, apesar de não ter conseguido vender a Cemig, principal empresa estatal mineira quando foi governador, Zema afirmou que vendeu 118 empresas e participações do governo de Minas Gerais durante os anos em que esteve à frente do estado.

O ex-governador citou entre os ativos negociados participações na Light e na Companhia Brasileira de Lítio, além da privatização da Copasa. Segundo ele, uma mudança na Constituição mineira exigia o apoio de três quintos da Assembleia Legislativa para a venda de estatais e essa maioria foi alcançada no caso da companhia de saneamento.

“Ficou faltando uma empresa só. Todas as outras foram vendidas. E, lembrando um detalhe importantíssimo durante a minha gestão, a empresa de saneamento de Minas, que é a Copasa, e a empresa de energia de Minas, que é a Cemig valorizaram estrondosos 300%, porque não teve roubalheira, não teve corrupção. Foi uma gestão profissional, valorizando o patrimônio do mineiro, e eu vou fazer o mesmo no Brasil”, disse o candidato.

Zema afirmou que não pretende, inicialmente, aumentar a idade mínima para aposentadoria. Segundo o candidato, eventuais mudanças na Previdência dependerão também do aumento da expectativa de vida da população e de uma maior formalização no mercado de trabalho.

Questionado sobre possíveis alterações nas regras para trabalhadores rurais e militares, Zema afirmou que as decisões dependerão do resultado do ajuste fiscal que pretende implementar, se eleito. O candidato disse que pretende reduzir gastos, combater fraudes e corrupção e melhorar a eficiência da administração pública.

“A aposentadoria vai depender muito disso. Agora, o brasileiro já trabalha muito. Eu não quero o brasileiro trabalhando mais. Eu quero a renda do brasileiro aumentando”, afirmou Zema.

O candidato à Presidência prometeu aumentar em dez vezes o número de escolas de tempo integral no país. Segundo ele, a meta de longo prazo é universalizar o modelo.

Zema citou sua gestão como governador e afirmou que o número de escolas com ensino médio em tempo integral passou de cerca de 70, quando assumiu o governo, para mais de 800 ao deixar o cargo.

“Me comprometo, como eu fiz em Minas, dez vezes. Dez vezes”, afirmou ao ser questionado sobre qual seria sua meta para os quatro anos de mandato. “Países desenvolvidos, países sérios, a criança fica na escola o dia todo."

Zema foi questionado sobre a redução de investimento em informação e inteligência de R$ 533 milhões para R$ 200 milhões no estado de Minas Gerais durante a sua gestão. Segundo o Anuário Brasileiro de Segurança Pública. Respondeu que o governo foi marcado por quedas contínuas na criminalidade.

O ex-governador disse que considera a rubrica importante, e que, durante a realização de levantamentos de informação, o investimento pode “cair numa outra sigla e não ser considerado”. Como exemplo, citou uma comparação entre a compra de viaturas e serviços de inteligência.

Ainda segundo Zema, os investimentos em segurança pública em Minas Gerais cresceram ao longo do seu governo. “Tem outra questão também: quem constrói uma casa neste ano, no ano que vem a despesa com construção diminui. Talvez a implantação tenha sido no início do meu governo e depois foram manutenções”, argumentou. “Enquanto a despesa foi alta, você estava adquirindo o sistema, implantando — é lógico que ela vai cair depois. Mas o que interessa é o resultado.”

Outra pergunta foi sobre a Operação Rejeito, ação da Polícia Federal deflagrada durante o governo do candidato, que identificou uma organização criminosa que atuou para obter vantagens econômicas por meio de crimes ambientais, lavagem de dinheiro e corrupção.

“Fica aqui o meu repúdio a esses bandidos que, além de estarem recebendo dinheiro, estavam destruindo o meio ambiente”, afirmou. “Quero que tudo seja apurado e que esses bandidos mofem na prisão."

Na avaliação de Zema, um estado com mais de 300 mil funcionários está sujeito a ter “algumas frutas podres”. Ele afirmou que seu governo tomou “todas as medidas”, defendendo “investigação, polícia, prisão, [e] punição”.

Romeu Zema, de 61 anos, é empresário e ex-governador de Minas Gerais. Depois de se afastar da gestão das empresas da família para entrar na política, foi eleito governador em 2018 e reeleito em 2022. Agora, candidato do Novo à Presidência, tenta se apresentar como uma alternativa ao bolsonarismo, embora tenha apoiado Jair Bolsonaro nas duas eleições anteriores. Leia o perfil do candidato.

Zema se aproximou da família Bolsonaro em 2018, mas passou a se distanciar e, mais recentemente, intensificou as críticas a Flávio Bolsonaro, dizendo que é preciso unir a direita para derrotar Lula. Nas pesquisas, aparecia com 2% das intenções de voto na Quaest de 14 de agosto.

Romeu Zema, César Tralli e Renata Vasconcellos nos Estúdios Globo, no Rio de Janeiro — Foto: Globo/ Manoella Mello

O discurso de Zema mantém como eixos a redução do tamanho do Estado, reformas administrativas e críticas ao PT e ao STF. Zema defende mudanças nas regras para ministros da Corte e já entrou em conflito público com Gilmar Mendes.

No governo de Minas, das 12 promessas feitas em 2022, quatro foram cumpridas integralmente , cinco parcialmente e três não foram cumpridas.

O plano de governo de Romeu Zema para a Presidência, registrado no TSE , propõe uma agenda de forte redução da participação do Estado na economia, flexibilização das relações trabalhistas e endurecimento das políticas de segurança pública.

Entre as medidas estão a privatização de estatais, mudanças na Previdência e na CLT, ampliação do acesso a armas, redução da maioridade penal, mudanças no funcionamento do STF e alterações no sistema político e na política externa.

Veja as principais propostas de Zema, registradas no TSE:
